question.html:
A stationary radium-226 nucleus decays into a radon-222 nucleus through alpha-decay. 

We are given the following data about this decay:

Total binding energy of radon-222 nucleus: 1708.179 MeV

Binding energy per nucleon for alpha-particle: 7075.2 keV

Energy released during the decay: J

a. State what is meant by the binding energy of a nucleus.

  [1]

b.

i. Calculate the binding energy per nucleon for the radium-226 nucleus.

  [4]

ii. The dot on the diagram shows A, the nucleon number and E, the binding energy per nucleon of the nuclide. Sketch a graph to show how binding energy per nucleon varies with nucleon number.

  [2]

iii. Plot, on the diagram in part (b) (ii), the position of the radium-226 nucleus.

  [1]

c. Through alpha-particle scattering experiments, Rutherford was able to construct a model of the atom. Outline this model.

  [2]
